---
title: "3 · Modeling with limpa"
---

[limpa](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/limpa.html) models the
**dropout curve** — the relationship between a peptide's underlying abundance and its probability
of being missing — then uses it to summarize peptides into proteins and to impute missing values
in a way that respects that missingness mechanism. This is what makes a principled differential
analysis possible on sparse single-cell data.

## Installation

```r
# Bioconductor
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("limpa")
```

## From quantification table to `EList`

limpa works on a limma-style `EList` with three parts: an expression matrix (`E`), a peptide/gene
annotation table (`genes`), and a sample metadata table (`targets`). In this project those are
built from the FlashLFQ `QuantifiedPeptides.tsv` by helper functions in
`MainManuscript/CustomScripts.R`:

```r
library(limpa)
source("MainManuscript/CustomScripts.R")

df   <- read.csv("Data/DiversePtms/QuantifiedPeptides.tsv", sep = "\t", row.names = NULL)
df   <- df[grepl("Homo sapiens", df$Organism), ]
df   <- CleanAmbiguousPeptides(df)          # resolve human/contaminant ambiguity

intensity_cols <- grep("^Intensity_", colnames(df), value = TRUE)
expr    <- GetExpressionMatrix(df, intensity_cols)   # log2, zeros -> NA
genes   <- GetGeneTable(df)                          # PeptideSequence / BaseSequence / ProteinGroup / Gene
targets <- GetMetaDataTdpStratified(expr)            # Group / TDP_Lvl / Donor / PMI / Age / Sex

y.peptide <- structure(list(E = expr, genes = genes, targets = targets), class = "EList")
```

## Dropout-curve modeling, summarization, and imputation

```r
# 1. Fit the dropout curve
dpcfit <- dpc(y.peptide)
plotDPC(dpcfit)

# 2. Summarize peptides to proteins (information-aware)
y.protein <- dpcQuant(y.peptide, "ProteinGroup", dpc = dpcfit, verbose = TRUE)

# 3. Impute peptide-level missing values for occupancy analysis
y.peptide.imputed <- dpcImpute(y.peptide, "PeptideSequence", dpc = dpcfit, verbose = TRUE)
```

`dpcQuant()` propagates per-measurement standard errors into `y.protein$other$standard.error`,
which the PTM-occupancy analysis later combines when normalizing modified peptides to their parent
protein.

::: {.callout-note}
These steps are slow. `MainManuscript/analysis.R` caches `y.peptide`, `dpcfit`, `y.protein`, and
`y.peptide.imputed` as `.rds` files in `Data/`; delete those cache files to force a full rerun.
:::

> **Paper:** [*Quantification and differential analysis of mass spectrometry proteomics data with
> probabilistic recovery of information from missing values*](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.28.651125v1.full)
